operator_io_quirks: Sales has 6,715,221 rows; read_schema must sample via rowid % k (max_rows_per_table=300000) and still report original_sizes=6715221.
Sales.SalesID distinct=200000 but rows=6715221: PK values repeat in the original (not a true unique key in practice); sample_fresh_primary_keys will drop many rows.
Sales FK columns (SalesPersonID/CustomerID/ProductID) have distinct 22/230/80 vs parent sizes 22/19759/504: FK values are heavily skewed, not uniform over parents.
All FKs are declared with ON UPDATE/DELETE CASCADE; writer must create DDL with foreign_keys pragma OFF (upstream default) so cascade never fires during insert.
Employees.MiddleInitial is TEXT with lowercase single-char samples ('e','l','a') while Customers.MiddleInitial is uppercase ('A','B','C'): same column name, different case convention across tables.
Customers.MiddleInitial null_rate=0.422 (nullable, 27 distinct); Employees.MiddleInitial null_rate=0.0 despite being declared null.
Products.Price is REAL, nullable, distinct=254, samples include 0.0 and 189.6: Number fuzzer with scale from 'real' (no args) -> default scale, range [-10^s,10^s].
All declared types are plain INTEGER/TEXT/REAL (no length args, no (a,b) args): Number scale defaults, String length defaults to 20.
Table/column names are mixed case (Customers, FirstName, SalesPersonID); generated SQL must double-quote with original spelling.
Sales.Quantity distinct=88 with samples up to 810: integer values well outside any small range; Number fuzzer will produce values in [-10^s,10^s].
No composite PKs, no self-FKs, no dangling FKs, no unique/check constraints beyond PKs: simplest possible schema shape.
Sales is the only child table; Customers/Employees/Products are all level-0 parents, Sales is level 1.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INTEGER PKs (CustomerID, EmployeeID, ProductID, SalesID) with default scale: fresh draws uniform in [-10^s,10^s] then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PKs will be large random ints, not 1..N.

String fuzzer on FirstName/LastName/MiddleInitial/Name: 5 original samples + literal pool, p=0.2 fresh random strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contaminate; names become implausible gibberish -> likely FN on name-equality queries.

Number fuzzer on Products.Price (REAL, no args): scale defaults, values in [-10^s,10^s] with +-0.01/+-0.02 perturbation; original prices are 0..190, so TS prices are wildly out of range -> FN on price-range predicates.
Number fuzzer on Sales.Quantity: same wide range; original 1..~810, TS may emit negatives or huge ints -> FN on quantity predicates.

FK fill: Sales.SalesPersonID draws from Employees.EmployeeID final values (22 rows, PK-filtered); Sales.CustomerID from Customers.CustomerID (19759); Sales.ProductID from Products.ProductID (504). With replacement, so Sales rows concentrate on few parents -> join cardinalities skewed.

choose_table_sizes: w.p. 0.5 flat rand_lin (30*u + int(u2*200)) else level sizes (level0=1+30u, level1 x4 capped 2500); Sales (level 1) gets up to 2500 rows, parents up to ~30-2500 -> Sales may be smaller than Customers, inverting the original 6.7M vs 19k ratio.
PK dedup on Sales.SalesID: since Number fuzzer draws from a wide range, collisions rare, but max_l0 reuse after ~30 fresh draws can cause PK duplicates -> rows dropped, Sales shrinks further.

No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python: nullable MiddleInitial and Price may get NULLs from String/Number samplers (Base drops None elements but fresh draws never NULL) -> actually NULLs only via FK-to-empty-parent; here parents non-empty so NULLs rare.

Missing ties/duplicates: original Sales has 6.7M rows with only 200k distinct SalesID and 22/230/80 distinct FKs -> many ties; TS generates <=2500 rows with near-unique PKs -> FP on GROUP BY / DISTINCT / COUNT queries that depend on tie multiplicity.

Literal pool from train SQL will seed FirstName/LastName/Name with real names and Price/Quantity with real numbers; p=0.2 fresh means ~80% of values come from pool+originals -> some plausibility preserved, but contaminate and perturbation still inject noise.
